explanation: The islands the sugar planters took in the seventeenth century had been emptied in the sixteenth. No indigenous labour force was left in the Greater Antilles to compel, and the Lesser Antilles had never held one of the size a plantation economy needed. The planters therefore bought their labour and shipped it in. The cause here is an absence, and it is no weaker for that. The planters took the decision to import Africans in those numbers against the emptiness the previous century had made.
